rows.purpose: The solver enters a full-model workspace and reads the saved session and working context.
rows.reason: F-SESSION and charter sections 4 and 5 retain opening and resuming work through one application entry. The browser experiment and its G1/G2 entry modes become the new shell under the owner design decision of 2 October 2026, section 7.
requirements: Use one entry and one workspace, with direct context resume and an explicitly labelled practice copy of the full model.
Adopt coherent state, workspace and protection revisions before enabling actions; expose loading, unavailable and stale states.
Load the existing model identity without dropping any of the 259,800 labels or 1,200 legal generators.
rows.notes: These are source-based disposition proposals, not Windows, input-device or performance evidence. Flows remain provisional under dispositions/README.md; stage 2.3 determines the interaction, layout and keys.

rows.purpose: The solver finds every available operation and invokes it from the keyboard or a searchable command catalogue.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE and charter E5 require keyboard reachability through the command table, while charter section 5 records that the 0.4 command list was hard to understand. The owner design decision of 2 October 2026, section 5, keeps every command available despite soft key disclosure.
requirements: Route every invocation through the shared command ID, contexts and engine availability, including operations previously excluded as form-only.
Use human-reviewed glossary wording and task context while retaining access to all commands at every disclosure level.
Editor, modal and IME ownership and the non-repeating commit gate apply to catalogue activation as well as physical keys.

rows.purpose: The solver explicitly selects a named set of keys suited to the current orbit and work.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE and solving-workflow section 4.3 retain explicit keyboard sets with stable meanings. The chooser and activation become one command-layer interaction in the new shell under charter section 4.
requirements: Show the candidate set, orbit, purpose, fixed caps and buffer context before explicit activation.
Clear held input across a set change and require release before a key can act in the new context.
Preserve per-orbit context and access to every legal generator; selecting a set never selects or executes a macro.

rows.purpose: The solver chooses a working orbit using its exact structural and orientation properties.
rows.reason: F-TARGET and solving-workflow sections 2 and 4.2 require explicit orbit choice with continuity of work. The structural chooser is redesigned under charter section 5 rather than inheriting the browser dialog.
requirements: Distinguish orbit ID, structural description and certified collateral-dependent stage order; do not treat ID order as solve order.
C-02: Change the active orbit and its workspace context atomically, including follow-up focus or Next fields, with no change on failure.
Retain the outgoing draft and choices, resolve resumed identities in current state, retain current global protection and invalidate execution permission.
Only the solver activates an orbit; suggestions and structural previews remain analysis.

rows.purpose: The solver explicitly returns to the previously used keyboard set.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE and solving-workflow section 4.3 retain explicit switching of stable key sets. The browser shortcut becomes a command in the common keyboard model required by charter E5.
requirements: Identify the previous set and handle its absence without silently choosing a substitute.
Reset held input when returning and retain the set's saved mappings and purpose.
Returning to keys cannot execute a turn, choose a macro or restore old protection.

rows.purpose: The solver gives a keyboard set a recognisable personal name.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE and solving-workflow section 4.3 retain editable working sets. The name editor is rehosted through the workspace command layer defined by charter section 4.
requirements: Persist the display name separately from the stable set ID and its fixed cap mappings.
Validate names before writing and leave the previous name and key meanings intact on rejection.
Use the same name wherever the set is shown, without changing its active orbit or executing anything.

rows.purpose: The solver explicitly switches to an orbit-specific keyboard set for the current solving task.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE, F-COMPOSE and F-ENDGAME use the task sets recorded in solving-workflow section 4.3. The 0.4 suffix shortcuts are redesigned as command IDs; their old keys and set presentation are not a 1.0 design decision.
requirements: Retain explicit access to buffer, insertion, macro-composition and endgame key-set purposes.
Make the active set and its meaning visible, clear held input on switching and preserve per-orbit choices.
A task-set switch changes input context only; it cannot select or execute a solving macro.

rows.purpose: The solver explicitly selects or releases one fixed cap as the Grip for later turns.
rows.reason: F-COMPOSE and solving-workflow section 4.3 retain Grip as one of the two physical turn-editor actions. Physical and on-screen entry share this purpose and are redesigned through the shell input model of charter section 4.
requirements: Use explicit canonical caps and fixed saved mappings; camera, filter or piece motion never changes a key meaning.
Selecting a Grip remains separate from inspection, target assignment and camera movement and never changes mechanical state.
Ambiguous simultaneous grips and unassigned slots cannot yield a turn; clear input at focus, modal, busy and key-set transitions.
Keep all legal generators reachable despite limited visible key slots.

rows.purpose: The solver chooses whether an explicit Grip is held or latched between key presses.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE and F-COMPOSE retain the Grip input modes recorded in solving-workflow section 4.3. The browser-only selector becomes a consistent preference and input-context command under charter section 4.
requirements: Expose the effective mode consistently for physical and on-screen input and retain the chosen preference.
Changing mode clears held, latched and pointer grips and cannot reinterpret a held key as a new action.
Key repeat must not toggle the mode or issue extra turns.

rows.purpose: The solver finds existing macros by orbit, purpose and searchable descriptive or exact effect information.
rows.reason: F-MACRO and solving-workflow section 6 retain a macro base organised by orbit and use. Opening, searching and filtering its catalogue are one discovery purpose redesigned under charter section 5 and the human-solve boundary in section 7 of the workflow.
requirements: Show the orbit, use, provenance and checked or unchecked effect status without treating a match as execution permission.
The solver chooses the macro; search and classification cannot generate or automatically select a solving macro.
Search remains responsive and results stay bound to the current library and context revisions.
Use the shared command table and keyboard route for catalogue access and selection.

rows.purpose: The solver explicitly enters a legal cap turn into a draft phase or the committed puzzle.
rows.reason: F-COMPOSE and F-EXECUTE retain explicit Grip/Twist input, with separate draft and live semantics in solving-workflow section 4.1. The browser controls are redesigned while the full legal-generator and protection contract of charter section 2 remains binding.
requirements: X-02: Live-turn receipts and status refreshes must not scan checkpoint label blobs or grow in cost with checkpoint count; verify on synthetic long histories.
Draft input changes only the chosen ordered phase; a live turn is a complete operation checked against current protection without borrowing future Cleanup.
Use one explicit fixed Grip, supported axis and inverse sign; preserve the finite legal witness and full collateral in chronological source-to-destination order.
Recheck current state identity and command gates; held-key repeat, busy, stale, text, modal and IME input cannot queue extra turns.
Report a committed turn as applied even if the display refresh fails, and retain draft and provenance on rejected input.

rows.purpose: The solver explicitly chooses the inverse direction of an on-screen cap turn.
rows.reason: F-COMPOSE and F-EXECUTE retain the solver's choice of legal turn direction in solving-workflow section 4. The inverse toggle is redesigned as part of the common input model, not automated, under the human-solve boundary in section 7.
requirements: Make the effective inverse direction clear before a turn and use the engine's exact legal inverse.
Physical and on-screen entry must agree on direction semantics without silently changing the selected cap or input destination.
Changing direction is a context action and cannot itself execute a turn.

rows.purpose: The solver decides whether a turn is live or draft and where draft input belongs in the operation.
rows.reason: The coarse claude:S5-44 row covers two purposes: execution destination and composition phase. Solving-workflow section 4.1 separates live execution from draft editing, while F-COMPOSE separately needs phase selection.

parts.purpose: The solver explicitly chooses whether later turns edit a draft or execute on the live puzzle.
parts.reason: F-COMPOSE and F-EXECUTE require the draft/live boundary in solving-workflow section 4.1. The destination selector is redesigned through the command table of charter section 4.
requirements: Make the effective destination unambiguous before turn input and persist it as work context.
Reset held input on changing destination; the selection itself cannot execute a turn.
Drafts never change committed labels; live turns receive complete-operation protection checks with no future draft allowance.

parts.purpose: The solver chooses which operation phase receives later draft turns.
parts.reason: F-COMPOSE and solving-workflow section 4 retain explicit Prepare, Macro and Cleanup composition. The phase selector is redesigned without choosing the operation for the solver.
requirements: Expose and retain the active draft phase and append later draft turns chronologically to that phase only.
Changing phase clears held input and invalidates any review affected by edits, without changing the live state.
Opening a phase editor and selecting the keyboard destination remain distinct commands with visible context.

rows.notes: claude:S5-44 appears in both parts because it describes both selectors; the two finer Codex rows identify their separate coverage.

rows.purpose: The solver inspects the exact effect and applicability of a macro they have selected.
rows.reason: F-MACRO and F-CHECK retain analysis of the solver's own selected macro under solving-workflow sections 4 and 7. The browser selection and effect display become a graphic inspection in the new shell under charter section 5.
requirements: Show the finite witness, full-model support, directed cycles, orientation, collateral and applicability with explicit evidence status.
Distinguish macro-body analysis from the complete operation and from current execution permission.
Selecting or inspecting a macro neither inserts it into a phase nor executes it; insertion remains an explicit command.
Invalidate stale effect displays when their macro version or context changes.

rows.purpose: The solver composes an operation by inserting a chosen macro into a named phase.
rows.reason: F-COMPOSE and solving-workflow section 4 retain Prepare, Macro and Cleanup assembled from the solver's chosen steps. The phase controls and drag/drop share that purpose and are redesigned, not deleted or automated, under the human-solve boundary.
requirements: Keep phase, selected macro version and append versus replace intent explicit and offer the same command through the keyboard.
Change draft steps only, retain an undoable previous draft and invalidate review and preview after a successful edit.
Validate complete input before changing any phase; rejected insertion leaves the previous draft and its provenance intact.
Preserve ordered finite witnesses and every collateral effect; insertion cannot execute a macro.

rows.purpose: The solver explicitly maps Grip keys to a chosen list of fixed canonical caps.
rows.reason: F-COMPOSE and F-NAVIGATE retain explicit cap capture under solving-workflow section 4.3. Editing the list and staging hosting, affecting or buffer caps serve the same mapping purpose, redesigned through the workspace command layer.
requirements: Distinguish hosting cells from the complete set of affecting caps and keep every legal generator accessible beyond the current captured subset.
Source helpers stage a candidate only; applying a validated mapping requires the solver's explicit action.
Persist canonical cap identities independently of camera, filtering and moving occupants and reset held input after capture.
Show Buffer A/B caps as derived from fixed positions, not from a mistaken identification of the buffers with their occupants.

rows.purpose: The solver reads exact support, cycles, orientation and collateral for the inspected macro or complete operation.
rows.reason: F-CHECK and charter S4 retain full-effect and witness inspection, and charter section 5 replaces text-heavy displays with accurate graphics. The 0.4 exact-effects dialog is redesigned while complete analysis stays full-model.
requirements: Label whether the effect is a macro body or the full Prepare/Macro/Cleanup operation and show its witness and reference.
Keep support, direction, orientation and protected conflicts exact on all labels, including filtered-out regions.
Declare truncation and unknown or unchecked details; a shortened display cannot imply that unshown pieces stay fixed.
Tie the result to the macro and context revisions, using the shared encoding and glossary required by the owner design decision of 2 October 2026.

rows.purpose: The solver configures personal keyboard mappings and preserves a portable copy of those mappings.
rows.reason: The coarse claude:S5-61 row combines configuration with file export, which have different validation and side effects. F-NAVIGATE retains keyboard editing and F-REUSE retains portable work under charter section 4.

parts.purpose: The solver edits or restores a candidate keyboard mapping and explicitly saves it.
parts.reason: F-NAVIGATE and solving-workflow section 4.3 retain editable stable key meanings. Charter E5 and the command table require those keys to invoke the same gated commands as other inputs.
requirements: Represent commands, Grip and Twist bindings and per-set overrides in one validated configuration with stable command IDs.
Restoring defaults stages a candidate; saving is explicit and atomic, and rejection preserves the existing bindings.
Keep text, editor, modal, IME, busy and non-repeating commit rules effective regardless of user mappings.
Reset held input when applying bindings and retain a keyboard path to all commands and legal generators.

parts.purpose: The solver exports an identified keyboard configuration for safekeeping or reuse.
parts.reason: F-REUSE retains the solver's reusable work and charter section 4 gives file actions to the command layer. The browser download of possibly unsaved form text is redesigned as a validated configuration export.
requirements: Identify whether the export contains a local draft or the saved effective mappings and validate it before producing the file.
Use an explicit version, stable command and set identities and model compatibility information.
Export key configuration only, without authentication tokens, session paths or unrelated personal state; export cannot apply mappings or execute commands.

rows.notes: claude:S5-61 covers both parts; codex:S5-17 is a staging step of configuration, not a separate automation decision. Export of unsaved form text must be distinguishable from the saved-keymap export in U3-126 and U6-010.

rows.purpose: The solver records an explicit finite macro of their own for later analysis and reuse.
rows.reason: F-MACRO and F-REUSE retain entering and saving the solver's own macros under solving-workflow sections 4 and 7. The browser JSON form is redesigned, while charter section 2 preserves legal witnesses and complete collateral.
requirements: Validate the entire explicit finite recipe against the unchanged model before saving a versioned personal macro.
Retain name, purpose, provenance and finite legal witness with the full action; do not save a filtered target-only effect.
Provide undoable workspace editing and clear validation feedback without committing the macro to the puzzle.
The program accepts the solver's macro and returns its analysis; it cannot choose or generate a solving macro.

rows.purpose: The solver records a recognisable name and purpose for an existing macro.
rows.reason: F-MACRO and F-REUSE use a macro base organised by orbit and use in solving-workflow section 6. The browser metadata editor is redesigned through the shared workspace commands of charter section 4.
requirements: Keep the stable macro identity, version and witness separate from editable display metadata.
Validate and persist name and purpose atomically and reflect the same metadata in search and inspection.
A metadata edit cannot change mathematical effect, select another macro or imply a fresh safety review.

rows.purpose: The solver compares the exact actions of two macros they choose.
rows.reason: F-MACRO and F-CHECK retain analysis of the solver's own macros under solving-workflow section 7. The comparison display is redesigned according to charter section 5 and M3, which keep exact facts and evidence separate from scores and permission.
requirements: Compare explicit macro versions on the full model and report full equality, inverse relation and orbit-local equality separately.
Include collateral and finite witness provenance; local agreement cannot be presented as whole-model equivalence.
Comparison is read-only analysis and cannot choose a winner, output a solving macro or grant execution permission.

rows.purpose: The solver changes working focus between composition, reference inspection and key use without losing context.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE supports the shared piece-focused workflow in solving-workflow section 6. The browser Work/Reference/Keys tab arrangement is redesigned under the owner design decision of 2 October 2026, section 6, which requires only linked Global and Local views.
requirements: Retain roles, target, buffers, draft, reference and protection across changes of working focus.
Integrate the work and reference purposes with the two linked views; do not require three mutually exclusive geometric views.
Focus changes use a keyboard route and never silently rebind Grip keys or modify the mechanical state.

rows.purpose: The solver explicitly names the current piece identity and its intended fixed destination.
rows.reason: F-TARGET and F-FIND retain explicit piece and destination choice in solving-workflow section 4. The typed Current dialog is redesigned while keeping inspection separate from assignment under section 4.3.
requirements: Validate typed identity and position kinds and the unchanged model limits, and distinguish Home from an explicitly chosen destination.
C-02: Store focus, active orbit and corresponding workspace context atomically, preserving all previous context if validation or saving fails.
Target assignment cannot choose or insert a macro, assign a Grip, move the camera or execute.
Resolve identity locations in current state and invalidate reviews affected by role or target changes.

rows.purpose: The learner inspects representative pieces to understand hosting, affecting caps and orientation structure.
rows.reason: F-LEARN and charter S3 retain exploration of real structure on the full model. The example selectors are redesigned as task-led learning under the owner design decision of 2 October 2026, section 7, rather than separate G1/G2 entry profiles.
requirements: Use verified representative identities from the unchanged model and show their actual hosting and affecting structures.
Loading an example changes chosen inspection or work context only and cannot import practice state or choose a solving macro.
C-02: If an example becomes Current in another orbit, adopt its orbit and workspace focus atomically while preserving outgoing context.
Learning uses the shared workspace or an explicitly labelled practice copy, without touching an existing solve.

rows.purpose: The solver locates and inspects the bookmarked next piece without activating it.
rows.reason: F-FIND and F-TARGET retain a locked Next and separate inspection from target activation in solving-workflow sections 3.3 and 4.3. The browser locate control is redesigned as an explicit view aid allowed by section 7.
requirements: Track Next by immutable identity and resolve its current cells against the shared state revision.
Leave Current, destination, buffers, protection and draft unchanged when locating Next.
Camera movement is an explicit locate action; a missing or stale bookmark gives a recoverable error rather than selecting another piece.

rows.purpose: The solver locks a chosen identity as Next and explicitly decides whether to replace an existing bookmark.
rows.reason: F-TARGET and solving-workflow sections 3.3 and 4.2 give the solver's locked Next priority. The bookmark control is redesigned without turning an explained candidate into an automatic target choice.
requirements: Store an identity bookmark separately from Current, fixed destination and mechanical protection.
Require explicit replacement of an existing Next and retain it across per-orbit work and interruption.
Pinning cannot activate the piece, choose a macro, change protection or execute anything.

rows.purpose: The solver explicitly releases the locked Next bookmark.
rows.reason: F-TARGET and solving-workflow sections 3.3 and 4.2 retain the solver's control over continuation. The clear action is redesigned through the workspace command layer, not as automatic selection of a replacement.
requirements: Clear only the Next bookmark and preserve Current, the destination, draft and protection.
The absence of Next may expose explained candidates but cannot silently activate one.
Reflect the cleared bookmark consistently across the shared context and both views.

rows.purpose: The solver explicitly makes the locked Next identity the current work target.
rows.reason: F-TARGET and solving-workflow section 4.2 retain explicit continuation, including a locked Next in another orbit. The browser activation control is redesigned while the solver remains the actor under the human-solve boundary.
requirements: Resolve the bookmarked identity in current state and require explicit activation; refuse an absent bookmark.
C-02: Switch orbit, restore its workspace and set focus as one atomic operation, retaining the outgoing draft and choices.
Keep current global protection, invalidate prior execution permission and remove stale effect overlays.
Activation cannot select a solving macro or execute a move.

rows.purpose: The solver declares a legal reference word and may explicitly save a selected macro in that reference.
rows.reason: claude:S5-30 covers both reference editing and saving a transformed macro, while codex:S5-25 covers reference editing only. F-COMPOSE and F-REUSE give these different purposes separate redesigned decisions under solving-workflow sections 4 and 7.

parts.purpose: The solver explicitly declares the legal reference word used by their work context.
parts.reason: F-COMPOSE and solving-workflow sections 3.3 and 4 retain a verified common reference. The reference editor is redesigned without searching for a solving macro or choosing a frame for the solver.
requirements: Validate the full finite legal word and its model identity before saving; an empty word retains the canonical-reference meaning.
Keep reference, roles and desired frame relations explicit and distinguish verified, unknown and unchecked evidence.
Changing the reference invalidates dependent reviews and execution permission without moving puzzle labels.

parts.purpose: The solver explicitly saves a reference-transformed copy of a macro they have selected.
parts.reason: F-REUSE and solving-workflow section 7 allow analysis and reuse of the solver's own macros. This is a requested transformation of chosen input, not the program choosing a solving macro.
requirements: Require an explicit macro version, reference word and save action; validate all input before any related workspace write.
Preserve chronological R inverse / Macro / R, its complete finite legal witness and every collateral effect in a new macro record.
Retain source macro and reference provenance, analyse the complete result and require a fresh review before any later execution.
The transform cannot apply itself to the puzzle or retarget the solver's work.

rows.notes: The transformation portion of claude:S5-30 also describes codex:S5-26, independently inventoried as U5-031 and left an open correspondence candidate. Both units decide that purpose consistently; inventory correspondences remain unchanged.

rows.purpose: The solver inspects and manages the locked Next bookmark through explicit actions.
rows.reason: F-TARGET and solving-workflow sections 3.3 and 4.2 retain a solver-owned continuation bookmark. The browser Next menu is redesigned as access to the shared locate, replace, clear and activate commands.
requirements: Show the bookmarked identity and its resolved current position, with a clear absent state.
Keep locating, replacing, clearing and activating distinct commands and apply their individual gates.
Explain that a bookmark is neither protection nor execution permission; opening its actions cannot change puzzle or work state.

rows.purpose: The solver explicitly saves a chosen macro as a new copy conjugated by their reference word.
rows.reason: F-REUSE and solving-workflow section 7 retain requested transformations of the solver's own macros. The browser reference-transform action is redesigned with complete-witness preservation under charter section 2.
requirements: Require an explicit selected macro version and legal reference word and validate both before committing reference or macro changes.
Save a new result with chronological R inverse / Macro / R, full collateral and finite legal witness, retaining source and reference provenance.
Do not mutate the source macro, silently retarget work or execute the transformed copy; later use requires a fresh review.
rows.notes: U5-029 part 2 covers the transformation in coarse claude:S5-30; U5-031 covers the unmatched fine codex:S5-26 row. The open correspondence remains an inventory issue, not another feature or a deletion.

rows.purpose: The solver adds a chosen piece and its intended arrangement to a working block.
rows.reason: F-TARGET and F-PROTECT use explicit block requirements under solving-workflow section 3.3. The browser add action is redesigned to express those conditions rather than merely inheriting the 0.4 button.
requirements: Record the stable identity, intended position or relations, reference and exact progress conditions with the new member.
Distinguish Home and referenced blocks and keep membership, completion and protection as separate facts.
Adding a requirement changes workspace intent only, invalidates affected reviews and cannot move a piece or automatically lock it.
Before execution show gains, losses and retained block members even when hidden by a work filter.

rows.purpose: The solver enters and edits the chronological finite steps of an operation phase.
rows.reason: F-COMPOSE and solving-workflow section 4 retain explicit Prepare, Macro and Cleanup editing. The JSON phase editor is redesigned while the complete legal-witness contract of charter section 2 remains unchanged.
requirements: Keep phase and chronological step order explicit and validate the complete edited recipe before storing it.
Change draft state only, retain undoable prior work and invalidate dependent review and preview after a successful edit.
Rejected edits preserve the previous draft, reference and recorded provenance.
The editor accepts solver-entered steps and cannot choose or generate a solving macro; temporary protected motion is judged in the complete draft.

rows.purpose: The solver protects the exact captured labels at a chosen fixed position.
rows.reason: F-PROTECT and solving-workflow section 3.3 require protection finer than whole orbits. The browser position-lock control is redesigned while retaining the exact-label preservation contract.
requirements: Capture the fixed position's full exact state from a current committed revision, distinguishing it from an identity lock.
Show the protection scope and Net or Strict policy and check all labels of hidden as well as visible objects.
Selecting or inspecting a predicted occupant cannot capture or alter a live position lock.
A protection edit invalidates affected review and preview; no analysis may silently remove the lock.

rows.purpose: The solver explicitly assigns fixed positions as buffers A and B.
rows.reason: F-COMPOSE and F-ENDGAME use the fixed buffer positions in solving-workflow sections 3.1 and 3.4. The browser role editor is redesigned while preserving the distinction between a buffer place and its changing occupant.
requirements: Validate distinct fixed A/B positions and their intended orbit before atomically saving the roles.
Show the buffers' current occupants separately and retain the fixed positions as pieces move.
Role changes invalidate dependent reviews, setup analyses and execution permission without relocating or selecting a macro.
Use the same buffer and reference context in both linked views and every operation tool.

rows.purpose: The solver reverses a draft edit without undoing a committed puzzle operation.
rows.reason: F-COMPOSE and the no-work-loss bar in charter E4 retain recovery of preparation work. The browser-window-only thirty-entry undo stack and its sequential phase writes are redesigned within workspace ownership under charter section 4.
requirements: Make draft undo distinct from journal undo and restore the affected phases and work context coherently in one workspace change.
Invalidate the review and preview for the restored draft and leave committed labels and current protection intact.
Define retention and recovery for draft edits across interruptions; handle an empty undo history without modifying work.
Failure during restoration preserves the previous draft rather than adopting only some phases.

rows.purpose: The solver compares a piece with its target, buffers and exact frames in the Local view.
rows.reason: F-FIND and F-CHECK retain local piece and target understanding from solving-workflow section 6. The owner design decision of 2 October 2026, section 6, requires a newly designed Local view visible together with Global.
requirements: Answer the Local question of whether the piece matches its target, using exact slots, occupants, orientation and reference frames.
Share one context and revision with Global, retaining fixed anchors for target, piece and buffers.
Show complete-operation effects and protection conflicts even when work or display filters exclude affected pieces.
Declare unknown frames and loading or stale information; inspection cannot assign targets or Grip mappings.

rows.purpose: The solver explicitly derives Cleanup as the inverse of their own Prepare phase.
rows.reason: F-COMPOSE and solving-workflow section 4 explicitly allow Cleanup to be the inverse of Prepare. Section 7 allows manipulation of the solver's own input, so this requested draft transformation survives as redesign rather than prohibited macro generation or automation.
requirements: Require an explicit solver action and derive the exact finite inverse by reversing chronological steps and signs.
Replace Cleanup only after full validation, retain undoable prior work and preserve draft provenance on rejection.
Do not choose a macro or setup or execute the result; invalidate prior safety results and review the complete new operation including collateral.

rows.purpose: The solver understands how the current piece, target and buffers relate across the whole 600-cell.
rows.reason: F-RELATE and solving-workflow section 6 retain whole-polytope relations. The owner design decision of 2 October 2026, section 6, requires a newly designed Global view linked and visible with Local, not the 0.4 projection panel.
requirements: Use the real model geometry and exact cell incidence to locate piece, target and buffers in one shared revision and context.
Explain projection and displayed relations in the UI's theory and glossary under charter M2 and the reduced M4 scope.
Distinguish shared cells, adjacency and navigation routes from legal move sequences; never substitute invented geometry while assets load.
Display full collateral and protection conflicts regardless of work filters, with colour carrying class rather than identity.

rows.purpose: The solver checks the complete operation, its goal, evidence and effect on protection before execution.
rows.reason: F-CHECK and solving-workflow sections 2 and 4.1 require analysis of complete Prepare/Macro/Cleanup on all labels. The review control and its text-heavy results are redesigned for charter S4 and the shared encoding in the owner design decision of 2 October 2026.
requirements: Review the immutable finite witness and complete chronological effect on all 259,800 labels, including filtered-out regions and collateral orbits.
Keep evidence, measured score, goal progress and execution permission separate; a legal operation with an unmet goal remains a distinct result.
Use Net checks at complete-operation boundaries or Strict checks at every primitive as requested; unchecked prefixes cannot be labelled safe.
Bind review to state, workspace, macro and protection revisions and invalidate it after relevant changes.
Keep analysis cancellable and the shell responsive; analysis cannot choose or execute a solving macro.

rows.purpose: The solver sees and inspects the actual full-model puzzle state in its geometric context.
rows.reason: F-FIND and F-RELATE retain viewing the puzzle itself. The separate browser Puzzle layout is redesigned into the Global and Local purposes required by the owner design decision of 2 October 2026, section 6, so the surviving visual purpose is not deleted.
requirements: Integrate actual puzzle geometry into the two linked views rather than adding a third competing view.
Render the unchanged full model and clearly distinguish committed labels from a read-only draft forecast.
Expose loading, renderer failure, stale and busy states and adopt coherent revision-labelled frames before enabling picking.
Keep labels and mechanical state owned by the engine; drawing, fitting or focusing a view never changes them.

rows.purpose: The solver stages a freshly reviewed complete operation for explicit execution.
rows.reason: F-CHECK and F-EXECUTE retain preview before commit under solving-workflow section 4 and charter S4. The browser Preview control becomes the shared command-layer preview path rather than an independent browser permission.
requirements: Accept only a current complete-operation review and bind preview to state hash, model, witness and workspace and protection revisions.
Show whole-operation collateral, protected conflicts and finite witness before execution, including filtered-out objects.
A forecast display is not execution authorization; stale, cancelled, resource-limited or unchecked results cannot enable commit.
Preview cannot mutate the puzzle or auto-execute; reuse or any relevant edit requires fresh validation.

rows.purpose: The solver dismisses temporary tools and returns keyboard focus to the ongoing work.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE retains deliberate dismissal and focus recovery. The browser action that hides a Local/Global/Puzzle deck is redesigned under the owner design decision of 2 October 2026, section 6, which keeps Global and Local visible together.
requirements: Dismiss transient tools or expanded inspection without removing either core linked view or losing shared work context.
Respect modal and editor ownership of Escape and restore focus to an existing valid origin or a defined workspace fallback.
Clear held input at a context transition, and do not equate visual dismissal with cancellation of a running job or preview.

rows.purpose: The solver explicitly commits the operation whose current complete effect they have previewed.
rows.reason: F-EXECUTE and solving-workflow sections 4 and 7 require one explicit solver action after a fresh preview. The browser Commit control is redesigned through the sole command layer of charter section 4 with the mathematical and protection checks of section 2.
requirements: X-02: Commit receipts and status refreshes must not scan checkpoint label blobs or grow in cost with checkpoint count; verify on synthetic long histories.
Recheck preview identity and revisions, full-state hashes, the immutable witness and all protected-object constraints immediately before commit.
Commit the full chronological permutation and journal witness in one transaction, with a durable command identity so retry cannot duplicate it.
Require explicit non-repeating activation through the shared busy and fresh-preview gates; the UI cannot independently grant permission.
Retain the successful command receipt if refresh fails and show applied with stale display rather than failure or an invitation to repeat.

rows.purpose: The solver discards pending execution permission without applying the proposed operation.
rows.reason: F-CHECK and F-EXECUTE need a safe way to abandon preview in solving-workflow section 4. The browser cancel control is redesigned through the shared command layer and its typed cancellation outcomes.
requirements: Cancel the identified pending preview and disable its execution permission while retaining the solver's reusable draft.
Leave committed state, journal and protection unchanged and show the authoritative cancellation result.
If cancellation races with a commit, resolve the durable command outcome and do not report an already applied operation as cancelled.

rows.purpose: The solver leaves a temporary dialog or local editor and recovers the previous input focus.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE and charter E4 retain safe interruption of editing without lost work. The shared HTML-dialog close behaviour is redesigned as shell focus and editor handling under charter section 4.
requirements: Distinguish abandoning local unsaved edits from saved workspace changes and requests already in flight.
Restore a valid previous focus, clear held or latched input and let modal or IME owners consume their keys.
Closing a surface cannot execute an action, erase a retained draft or imply that a running job has been cancelled.

rows.purpose: The solver stops a running analysis and learns its actual cancellation outcome.
rows.reason: F-CHECK and charter section 4 retain cancellable job handling with a responsive shell. The browser fire-and-report stop request is redesigned to distinguish a requested stop from an acknowledged cancellation under the command table's typed errors.
requirements: Associate cancellation with the active job identity and show pending, completed, cancelled and unknown outcome separately.
Analysis cancellation leaves committed state, protection and saved draft intact and prevents stale results from enabling execution.
Keep cancellation responsive and do not treat cancellation of analysis as rollback of an already committed operation.

rows.purpose: The solver defines and explicitly applies the piece set used for work display and interaction.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE and solving-workflow section 4.3 retain separate mechanical, work and reference scopes. The browser filter editor and apply action are redesigned while charter section 2 keeps mechanics independent of rendering.
requirements: Support explicit replace, intersect, union and subtract intent on a validated filter without narrowing full-model mechanics or protection.
Keep interactive work members separate from noninteractive references; hidden buffers may be reference-visible without becoming pickable or twistable.
Declare which expression and current revision are applied, and retain the previous work set on rejection.
Reveal complete-operation effects and protection conflicts through filtering; a filter change never rebinds keys or relabels pieces.
rows.notes: The preset and saved-expression loaders remain separate units U5-060 and U5-061, as in units.json; their open correspondence candidates do not authorise changing the inventory.

rows.purpose: The solver compares committed occupants with the predicted result of the complete draft.
rows.reason: F-CHECK and solving-workflow section 4 retain before/after review of complete effects. The browser display switches are redesigned for the two shared-revision views in the owner design decision of 2 October 2026, section 6.
requirements: Label committed and predicted state clearly and derive the forecast from a current complete-operation review without mutating labels.
Use the same operation, reference and revision in both linked views and invalidate the forecast after relevant edits.
A truncated cycle display marks unrepresented occupants unknown; it cannot imply no collateral outside shown cycles.
Forecast objects cannot use live picking, protection or target mutation paths; returning to committed display requires a coherent current frame.
rows.notes: U5-067 is an open inventory candidate because picking is disabled in predicted display; choosing a display and inspecting a committed sticker remain distinct purposes.

rows.purpose: The solver checks a proposed filter's membership and counts before applying it.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE and solving-workflow section 4.3 retain deliberate control of the work and interaction set. The browser count-preview button and raw result text are redesigned as understandable read-only feedback under charter section 5.
requirements: Evaluate the staged expression and composition operation against an identified current state and work-set revision without applying either.
Show exact counts and scope, including empty and invalid results, with glossary-consistent graphic feedback.
A later apply revalidates the current context; a count result cannot narrow mechanical analysis or enable a turn.

rows.purpose: The solver saves a named work filter for later reuse.
rows.reason: F-REUSE and solving-workflow section 4.3 retain saved sets with explicit live-query or frozen membership semantics. The browser save-current action is redesigned through the session store and workspace commands of charter section 4.
requirements: Identify exactly which applied or staged expression is being saved; do not silently save a different expression from the one the solver sees.
Record the name, query semantics and model compatibility while keeping frozen identities and frozen positions distinct from live queries.
Validate before atomically saving and leave active filter, mechanics and protection unchanged by the save action.

rows.purpose: The solver inspects an immutable piece identity and its current physical arrangement.
rows.reason: F-FIND and solving-workflow section 4.3 retain piece-focused tracking while separating inspection from role assignment. Diagram tokens and the browser pick callback are redesigned into revision-consistent inspection under charter section 5.
requirements: Resolve the stable identity in the current full-model state and show its current position, Home, slots and frame evidence.
Use coherent revision-tagged committed frames and reject stale, busy or forecast picks.
Inspection alone cannot change Current, destination, Grip, protection or camera; any assignment shortcut invokes a separate explicit command.
Provide keyboard inspection of the same objects and distinguish identity from fixed position and sticker label.
rows.notes: U5-067 inventories the committed-viewport gesture separately; the candidate correspondence is left open and both inspection purposes receive compatible requirements.

rows.purpose: The solver inspects a fixed position, its occupant and any exact protection conflict there.
rows.reason: F-FIND and F-CHECK retain fixed-position inspection under solving-workflow sections 3.3 and 4.3. Position sockets and conflict buttons share one inspection purpose redesigned with the owner's common encoding.
requirements: Keep the position identity fixed while resolving its current occupant, captured protected state and conflict at one shared revision.
Distinguish fixed position, occupant identity and desired frame with exact IDs and evidence status.
Inspection never unlocks the position, changes a target or grants permission, and a forecast cannot capture a live lock.
Make hidden conflicts inspectable despite the work filter and offer the same keyboard route as pointer activation.

rows.purpose: The solver inspects a chosen canonical cell and its role in the current structural context.
rows.reason: F-FIND and F-RELATE retain real cell relationships from solving-workflow section 4. The browser diagram markers are redesigned while section 4.3 keeps inspection separate from Grip assignment and camera movement.
requirements: Use unchanged canonical cell IDs and actual hosting, Home or affecting-cap incidence, shared between Global and Local.
Keep inspection, camera locate and cap capture as distinct explicit commands; selecting a cell cannot turn it.
Make the same cells reachable by keyboard and retain clear loading, absent and stale-context states.

rows.purpose: The solver finds and inspects saved work sheets for possible reuse.
rows.reason: F-REUSE and solving-workflow sections 4 and 4.1 retain the solver's own work sheets. The browser selector is redesigned to expose the sheet's context and fresh-review needs under charter section 5.
requirements: Identify each sheet's fixed phases, roles, reference and macro versions and compare them with current work.
Show missing, changed or incompatible inputs and protection conflicts without silently substituting macros or targets.
Browsing does not load or execute a sheet, and saved safety results are never current execution permission.

rows.purpose: The solver saves their current operation and work context as a named reusable sheet.
rows.reason: F-REUSE and solving-workflow section 4.1 retain phases, roles, reference and macro versions while rejecting reuse of old reviews. The browser save action is redesigned through session-store ownership in charter section 4.
requirements: Capture a coherent versioned sheet of the solver's fixed phases, roles, reference, macro versions and model identity.
Validate the complete input before atomic persistence, preserving the finite witnesses and full collateral.
A saved sheet is reusable work rather than execution authorization and cannot change puzzle state or auto-select future targets.

rows.purpose: The solver explicitly loads the fixed steps of a chosen work sheet into the current draft.
rows.reason: F-REUSE and solving-workflow section 4.1 retain confirmed reuse of the solver's own work. The browser load action is redesigned so mismatches are explained and every reuse receives a fresh review.
requirements: Inspect and confirm the selected sheet's exact phases, reference and macro versions before an undoable coherent draft change.
Keep Current, Next and current global protection under the solver's control; never silently retarget or restore old locks.
Expose role, target, version and protection mismatches and invalidate old review and preview permission.
Loading cannot choose a new solving macro or execute; failures leave the previous draft and context intact.

rows.purpose: The solver inspects and explicitly changes the scope and boundary policy of protection.
rows.reason: F-PROTECT and F-CHECK retain whole-orbit and finer protection with Net or Strict policy under solving-workflow sections 2 and 3.3. The browser checkboxes and sequential protect/prefix requests are redesigned as coherent policy editing under charter section 4.
requirements: Show orbit, position, identity and block protection scopes separately from selection and completion, including objects hidden by a filter.
Apply validated scope and Net/Strict policy coherently, preserving the old policy on failure and invalidating affected reviews.
Net checks the complete operation; Strict checks every primitive; unknown or unchecked prefix status is never safe.
Preserving an unsolved protected orbit means preserving its captured state; manual unlocking requires solver action and cannot be silently reversed on unchanged state.

rows.purpose: The solver explicitly releases the chosen scope of captured position locks.
rows.reason: F-PROTECT and solving-workflow section 3.3 retain solver control of exact position protection. The browser clear-all loop is redesigned as an explicit scoped command rather than removed or made automatic.
requirements: Show that the requested scope is all current position locks before explicit confirmation; leave whole-orbit, identity and other block policies intact.
Validate the current protection revision and perform a coherent release rather than silently stopping after only some per-position requests.
Invalidate review and preview after release and report the actual resulting scope.
No failed analysis, missing macro or exhausted candidate list may invoke this command automatically.

rows.purpose: The solver starts a work filter from a named structural or progress preset.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE and F-FIND use work membership under solving-workflow section 4.3. The browser preset buttons are redesigned as explicit query staging, retaining the solver's separate preview and apply choices.
requirements: Define presets using exact orbit, unsolved and orientation evidence rather than colour similarity or an empty result as completion.
Selecting a preset stages a visible query and does not apply membership or alter mechanical state, protection or keys.
Keep every legal generator reachable and reference-visible buffers distinct from interactive work members.
rows.notes: U5-048 also mentions these controls; units.json leaves that correspondence open, so this fine preset unit is decided separately without editing either inventory.

rows.purpose: The solver restores a saved work-filter definition for inspection and explicit application.
rows.reason: F-REUSE and solving-workflow section 4.3 retain reusable work sets. The browser saved-filter loader is redesigned to identify the saved query and its current meaning before apply.
requirements: Load the saved definition into a candidate without silently changing the active work filter.
Keep live query, frozen identities and frozen positions explicit, checking model compatibility and current membership as appropriate.
A missing or incompatible saved definition leaves the active set intact; later application uses current revisions and never narrows mechanics.
rows.notes: This loader is an open inventory candidate for U5-048 and stays separately decided. U3-124 persists saved definitions but does not itself inventory this loading interaction, so it is not asserted to have the same purpose.

rows.purpose: The solver chooses how much on-screen key guidance is visible while working.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE and F-LEARN retain key guidance under charter D7 and E5. The owner design decision of 2 October 2026, section 5, replaces G1/G2 strip defaults with soft disclosure while keeping all commands available.
requirements: Show the effective Grip, Twist and command meanings for the current context and allow experts to reveal all guidance.
Hiding guidance cannot disable commands, silently change key meanings or turn disclosure into an achievement gate.
Retain visible input context, including active set, Grip and draft/live destination, and suspend needless hidden rendering work.

rows.purpose: The solver restores a known camera framing without changing their solve or work context.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE and solving-workflow section 7 allow view aids. The browser camera reset is redesigned for the two views required by the owner design decision of 2 October 2026, section 6.
requirements: Define which camera is reset and keep target, buffers, drafts, filters and protection unchanged.
Maintain the shared revision and exact structural anchors when refitting the view.
Camera reset cannot rebind Grip keys, alter mechanical labels or represent a legal turn.

rows.purpose: The solver explicitly locates the current piece in the geometric views.
rows.reason: F-FIND and solving-workflow section 4 retain finding the piece and buffers. The browser first-hosting-cell camera action is redesigned as a linked view aid while section 4.3 keeps it separate from inspection and assignment.
requirements: Resolve Current's present hosting cells in the shared current revision and keep Home and destination distinct.
Handle absent or stale Current without choosing another target or a substitute grip.
Move presentation only after the explicit locate command; retain roles, key meanings, draft and protection.

rows.purpose: The solver explicitly locates an inspected piece or selected cell in its geometric context.
rows.reason: F-FIND and F-RELATE retain relating the inspected object to the whole structure in solving-workflow section 4. The browser locate control is redesigned without merging camera movement with inspection under section 4.3.
requirements: Identify whether the locate target is a selected canonical cell or the inspected identity's current hosting cells.
Resolve the target against the shared current revision and reflect it in linked Global and Local context.
Keep work roles, selected Grip, fixed mappings and puzzle labels intact; a missing target yields a recoverable error.

rows.purpose: The solver chooses a rendering presentation that keeps the puzzle structure legible and usable.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE retains view control and charter section 5 requires tunable graphics compatible with engineering and picking. The browser Adaptive/Full mesh/Point glyph choices are redesigned while charter section 2 requires the full-detail renderer gate.
requirements: Presentation options never change model identity, sticker labels, legal generators, protection or interaction scope.
Full-detail rendering of all 259,800 slots remains available and must pass the renderer gate in the shipped look; optional presentations cannot substitute for that evidence.
Do not enable picking until the rebuilt frame is coherent with the current labels and view revision.
Use the shared encoding and supported tuning ranges, keeping status and role meanings stable across presentations and themes.

rows.purpose: The solver selects a committed sticker to inspect its piece and may explicitly continue to target assignment.
rows.reason: F-FIND and F-TARGET retain picking as an inspection route under solving-workflow sections 4 and 4.3. The browser click and Shift-click conventions are redesigned without deciding 1.0 gestures or merging inspection with assignment.
requirements: Resolve the picked slot through its committed label to an immutable identity on one coherent state and view revision.
Reject stale, busy, predicted or noninteractive reference picks and distinguish an inspection result from execution permission.
Inspection does not assign Current or destination; opening assignment uses a separate explicit command and still requires the solver's choice.
Provide a keyboard path to the same inspect and assign purposes; picking cannot select a Grip or move the camera implicitly.
rows.notes: The inventory leaves U5-049 and U5-052 as candidate correspondences. Display choice and identity inspection are kept as their own units; this row covers the viewport entry to inspection without changing the inventory.

rows.purpose: The solver copies an unambiguous canonical identity for the inspected piece.
rows.reason: F-FIND, F-COMPOSE and F-REUSE use exact identities without repeated manual entry in solving-workflow sections 4 and 6. The browser clipboard command is redesigned with the typed identity distinctions required by charter M1 and the shared encoding.
requirements: Copy the acknowledged inspected identity with its canonical type prefix, distinguishing identity from position, slot and frame node.
Include or retain model compatibility information wherever the copied identity is reused and report clipboard success or failure accurately.
Do not include tokens or session paths or change work selection, protection or mechanical state.

rows.purpose: The solver reads the session identity and reaches commands for preserving, recovering and leaving work.
rows.reason: F-SESSION and charter section 4 retain session-store ownership and one shared application entry. The isolated-experiment dialog becomes session management in the new shell under the owner design decision of 2 October 2026, section 7.
requirements: Show session, model and build identity and clearly distinguish personal solving work from the full-model practice copy.
Expose undo, redo, checkpoints, reset, work export and safe exit through their shared commands and availability gates.
Keep evidence status and exact completion separate from legal execution, progress and synthetic practice.
Use a coherent current session report and accurate loading, busy, stale and error states without exposing private machine details.

rows.purpose: The learner explicitly loads a known legally witnessed practice task on an isolated full-model copy.
rows.reason: F-LEARN and charter D7 retain fixture tasks for learning and competence checks. The owner design decision of 2 October 2026, sections 5 and 7, requires fresh isolated data and a clearly labelled practice copy, so the E1 control is redesigned rather than deleted.
requirements: Use fresh isolated full-model practice and a verified explicit finite fixture witness, preserving its full collateral and synthetic provenance.
C-01: Loading a fixture cannot move captured protected positions, conflict with protected orbits or discard locks; retain the fixed protection regression in 1.0.
Require explicit load through the guarded command path and leave existing work intact on rejection.
Do not count practice as a human complete solve or have the program choose or execute the correction macro.
Retain an authoritative applied receipt even if the following display refresh fails.

rows.purpose: The solver undoes a committed operation while keeping state and history consistent.
rows.reason: F-EXECUTE and F-SESSION retain undo in solving-workflow sections 4 and 4.2 and charter E4. The browser session-button path is redesigned through the shared command layer while journal semantics remain the session-store responsibility.
requirements: X-02: Undo receipts and status refreshes must not scan checkpoint label blobs or grow in cost with checkpoint count; verify on synthetic long histories.
Use a guarded atomic journal operation with durable identity and coherent state and workspace revisions; do not confuse it with draft undo.
Reconcile protection through the authoritative undo contract and invalidate prior review, preview and forecasts.
Withdraw current achievements and pending celebration after undo but retain unlocked explanations and saved macros, as the owner design decision of 2 October 2026 requires.
Keep successful undo distinct from display refresh failure and prevent held-key repeats or retry from applying it twice.

rows.purpose: The solver explicitly reapplies an undone journal operation with coherent state and history.
rows.reason: F-EXECUTE and F-SESSION retain redo under solving-workflow section 4.2 and charter E4. The browser control is redesigned through the same guarded command path as other journal operations.
requirements: X-02: Redo receipts and status refreshes must not scan checkpoint label blobs or grow in cost with checkpoint count; verify on synthetic long histories.
Identify the authoritative redo operation and commit its complete legal witness and collateral atomically with the journal.
Apply current engine permission and protection rules and invalidate dependent reviews and forecasts after adoption.
Redo requires explicit non-repeating action and a durable identity; a successful redo with failed display refresh remains applied.

rows.purpose: The solver saves a named recovery point for the current puzzle and working context.
rows.reason: F-PROTECT and F-SESSION retain checkpoints in solving-workflow section 4.2 and the charter's protection flow. The browser name-and-save control is redesigned through the session store while preserving recoverability.
requirements: Capture a coherent full state, journal identity and working context under the unchanged model identity and store the name explicitly.
Preserve recovery checkpoints and existing preferences and give an authoritative durable save outcome.
Saving a checkpoint neither solves the puzzle nor grants execution permission; listing its metadata must not read full label blobs.

rows.purpose: The solver explicitly restores a chosen recovery point without losing a recoverable history.
rows.reason: F-SESSION and F-PROTECT retain consistent restore and interruption recovery in solving-workflow section 4.2. The browser restore control is redesigned through the session store under charter E4.
requirements: Validate the chosen checkpoint, complete state and model compatibility before transactional restoration; failure leaves current work intact.
Keep identity, labels, journal and restored work context coherent, preserve preferences and retain the recovery checkpoint.
Adopt protection according to the authoritative restoration contract and invalidate old previews, reviews and effect overlays.
Show which checkpoint and resulting history were restored and retain the applied receipt through refresh failure.

rows.purpose: The solver explicitly starts again from solved state with the previous work recoverable.
rows.reason: F-SESSION and AGENTS.md persistence rules retain transactional recoverable reset, and charter E4 forbids lost work. The browser reset control is redesigned in the single-entry workspace rather than deleted as experiment-only.
requirements: Identify the reset scope and obtain explicit confirmation before the guarded command changes state.
Validate first and reset state, history and work context coherently while retaining current preferences and the previous solve's recovery checkpoint.
A new or reset solved session must not blanket-lock orbits or be counted as a completed human solve.
Invalidate old review and preview and report committed reset separately from display refresh failure; injected failure leaves the original session recoverable.

rows.purpose: The solver exports their work definitions for safekeeping and later reuse.
rows.reason: F-REUSE and F-SESSION retain solver-owned macros, sheets, mappings and filters under charter section 4. The owner migration decision of 2 October 2026 chooses a locked database-copy importer, so this browser workspace download is redesigned as work export rather than treated as session migration.
requirements: Export a validated versioned definition bundle with model identity, stable command and macro IDs, finite witnesses and reference provenance.
Identify which saved workspace revision is exported and keep work definitions distinct from full puzzle state, journal or migration archive.
Include only intentional user work, with no authentication tokens, private paths, diagnostics or unrelated session data.
Any later reuse revalidates compatibility and current protection and cannot restore execution permission or execute a macro.
rows.notes: The native macro and keymap exports cover parts of this portability purpose, not the browser's whole workspace bundle. Path B migration remains an independent importer contract, and no migration export or source-session access is introduced here.

rows.purpose: The solver safely leaves the application and stops any engine process it owns while keeping work resumable.
rows.reason: F-SESSION and AGENTS.md process-ownership rules retain safe shutdown and recovery. Charter section 4 replaces the 0.4 runtime and process split, so the browser stop control is redesigned around the chosen 1.0 lifetime rather than deleted with the experiment host.
requirements: Resolve pending work by the authoritative wait-or-cancel policy before shutdown and keep committed journal and workspace recoverable for resume.
Stop only owned processes; an owned local engine uses EngineProcess authenticated health, graceful shutdown and parent-pipe recovery.
B-001: Idle, stalled or trickling request clients cannot extend graceful shutdown past its bound or force termination instead of orderly close.
Release input, rendering and job resources and report acknowledged shutdown separately from a request or unknown outcome.
Keep platform lifetime behind a narrow interface; safe exit does not prescribe the legacy browser, HTTP service or 0.4 process split for 1.0.
